newsitem.title: USA: Glickman sees no major changes to US farm program.
newsitem.headline: Glickman sees no major changes to US farm program.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said he remained concerned about introducing a safety net for family farms which might be hurt by the new seven year farm program but anticipated no major changes to legislation.

"We have no radical changes to that bill in mind. I just think we remain on a continuing basis concerned about the safety net and we will look at it," he said following a forum on rural issues at the Democratic National Convention.
"Whether that is in the form of improved crop insurance or improved risk management tools or whether it is looking at the substance of that bill again I'm not sure," he added.

Glickman noted that enrollment in the new program has been heavy. USDA reported last week that 98.8 percent of eligible acreage of wheat, feed grains, upland cotton and rice had been enrolled in the seven-year program.
"Farmers voted that they wanted to give this program a chance so I don't think for the time being you are going to see us going out and recommending any major changes," USDA's Glickman said.
